In \'Wide view\' mode, sets the exact tile grid on a wide screen or an external display (1 to 10 columns and 1 to 10 rows).
Sets the number of media grid columns in the right pane when the screen is split in \'Last opened\' and \'Multi-folder\' modes.
Sets the split between the folder pane (left) and the content pane (right) in 10% steps (10..90%) with the +/- buttons and presets. A live miniature above the control shows the real split.
On foldables, detects the laptop/tent posture (by default a hinge angle under 20° from upright, adjustable from 5° to 90°) and switches to a symmetric 50% / 50% split that matches the physical fold.
Fast scrolling through the gallery on the side of your choice (left/right). The grid follows the handle smoothly, pixel by pixel, or jumps by whole rows.

Hold any action card and drag it up or down to change its position or move it to the \'Hidden\' section.

Turn the phone sideways and folders and their contents show side by side, like on a tablet. The two-pane options show up too.

How long videos are, shown on their tiles: minutes and seconds (12:34) or with hours too (0:12:34).
A handle at the edge of a folder. Drag it to get anywhere in the folder in one move.
Smoothly: dragging the handle moves the grid pixel by pixel.
By whole rows: dragging the handle moves the grid in jumps, one row at a time.
Folders also show documents, archives and apps, not only photos and videos.
Folders holding only other files (for example Documents) also appear among the folders.
The Favorites folder disappears from the folder grid. Your favorite files stay marked.
Leave a folder and come back: it opens at the same place, also after the app is restarted.
When new files arrive, the folder scrolls to the top, where they show up.
Videos downloaded by NewPipe show up in this folder right away. Until the download ends, the tile shows its progress and stays locked.
Dragging over the grid selects a rectangle from corner to corner, or every file from the first to the last in order (linear).
Files are moved, renamed and so on in the order you tapped them.
The player skips the parts saved in the video by itself, for example sponsor segments.
Search results take the whole screen instead of only the left pane.
Describe a photo in your own words and Alexet finds the matching ones. It all runs on this phone.

Before a photo is shared, its location and camera data are removed.
Thumbnails sized to their tiles: sharper, but they use more memory.
Slide up or down on the right side of the video to change the volume.
Slide up or down on the left side of the video to change the brightness.
Hold a finger on the video to play it faster, at the chosen speed. Let go and it plays normally again.
Tap twice on the right or left side to jump forward or back by the chosen step.
A tap shows the controls, and they hide by themselves after the chosen time.
Tap a video twice to open it straight in the Alexet player. One tap still opens the external player.
Arrows at the sides of a photo switch to the previous or next one at once, without the slide.
GIFs play by themselves when opened. A tap in the middle pauses them.
File names show under the tiles in folders.
How many folders fit side by side in the folder grid. More columns, smaller tiles.
How many files fit side by side in a folder. On a tablet or an unfolded phone the two-pane count is used instead.
A button in the player shrinks the video into a small window over other apps.
A playing video or song goes on after you leave the app or turn the screen off, with controls in the notification. Not in private folders.
Tap the button at the top of the player and the video moves into a small window. It plays on over other apps, and you can drag it anywhere.
Leave the app or turn the screen off: the sound plays on, and the notification has play and pause. The picture is not decoded meanwhile, which saves battery.
Your chosen photos, one after another.
No photos. Tap to choose them.
Alexet has no access to your photos yet. Open the app, allow access, then add the widget again.
The same files and photos that look alike. The extra copies go to the trash.

Alexet looks for files with the same content, also under other names. With the AI index it also finds photos that look almost the same: bursts and copies in another resolution. In each group the best copy stays and the others are chosen for the trash; tap a photo to change that.
Without the AI index only identical files are searched.
Once a day at start, Alexet asks GitHub for a new version. It is the app\'s only use of the internet.
